title: Maintaining Proper Drainage Pitch
description: Proper pipe slope is critical for achieving self-scouring velocity in drainage systems. If a horizontal drain pipe has insufficient slope, liquid moves too slowly, allowing waste solids to settle and build up into blockages. Conversely, excessive slope can cause liquid waste to run ahead of solid waste, leaving dry solids behind inside the pipe. Plumbing codes specify required minimum slope based on pipe diameter to ensure solids remain suspended. Always check grade along the full length of the run with a level before securing pipe supports.

Maintaining Proper Drainage Pitch

Proper pipe slope is critical for achieving self-scouring velocity in drainage systems. If a horizontal drain pipe has insufficient slope, liquid moves too slowly, allowing waste solids to settle and build up into blockages. Conversely, excessive slope can cause liquid waste to run ahead of solid waste, leaving dry solids behind inside the pipe. Plumbing codes specify required minimum slope based on pipe diameter to ensure solids remain suspended. Always check grade along the full length of the run with a level before securing pipe supports.
